shift/task: A language model reads text and, at every step, predicts what comes next. Here the tokens are characters, and the text is hello.
shift/shift: So the inputs are h, e, l, l, and the targets are the same text shifted by one: e, l, l, o.
shift/scores: At each step, a linear layer turns the hidden state into one score for every token in the vocabulary: four here, h, e, l and o.
shift/softmax: Softmax turns the scores into probabilities for the next character. After reading h, this model gives e zero point five.
shift/memory: Look at steps two and three. Both read an l, but one must predict l and the other o. Only the memory, h, can tell them apart.
loss/step: Each step is a classification over the vocabulary, so its loss is cross-entropy. At step zero the target, e, got zero point five: the loss is minus its log, zero point six nine.
loss/all: Every step does the same against its own target: zero point nine two, zero point five one, and zero point two two.
loss/total: The loss for the whole text adds them up: two point three four. Divided by the four steps, that is about zero point five nine per step.
